interviews.speaker: Kai Brüning
interviews.why: Own interview of the process: full impact grid, MTPD, RTO, owner, emergency operation, resources and dependencies for change and release management.

activities.name: Change and release management (merged: request, risk analysis, approval, implementation, fallback plan, release scheduling and follow-up)

owner.name: Kai Brüning
owner.quote: It is a support process, and its process owner is the head of IT service management. The organisational unit is IT.

mtpd.speaker: Kai Brüning
mtpd.reason: Worst rating across categories never reaches the intolerable level 4 at any horizon, consistent with the stated grid.

rto.speaker: Kai Brüning
rto.reason: Process owner's decision, carried as stated; sits over an MTPD past the last horizon, so it is an RTO, not a recovery gap.

rpo.quote: IT systems. Atlassian Jira: RPO <24 h, RTO >168 h.
rpo.speaker: Kai Brüning
rpo.reason: No RPO was stated for the process itself; its change and release data live in Jira and Microsoft 365, both given RPO <24 h, so <24 h is the best fit.

conflicts.about: MTPD: the grid (2025) gives no MTPD within horizons by the method's rule, the draft says >168 h

sides.claim: no MTPD within horizons (the method's rule over the grid, 2025)
sides.speaker: method

conflicts.why: The method derives the MTPD from the grid; the other figure is the thing to explain.

gaps.what: The grid stays at level 1-2 everywhere, yet the interviewee says changes can have time-critical legislative or security requirements; a single urgently needed change could hurt far faster than the 168 h horizon shows. Also no RPO was stated for the process itself.
gaps.ask: Do you accept RPO <24 h for change and release data, and is an outage really tolerable up to and beyond 168 h even when a legally required or security-critical change is pending?
